neighbours.label: ' do' / ' does' right after 'How' in a direct how-question ('How do I ...', 'how do we ...')
fire: The form keeps rejecting my address. How do I change the postcode?
A reader writes in to ask: how do we stop the pipes from freezing?
The label has faded. How do you tell which jar is which?
My neighbour keeps asking me, how do they get the piano upstairs?
The kitchen is tiny. How does anyone cook for six in there?
The lecturer paused and asked, how do we measure something that small?
The box says nothing useful. How do I fold the tent back into the bag?
The guide is vague on one point: how does a visitor pay the toll?
quiet: The form keeps rejecting my address. What do I put in the postcode box?
A reader writes in to ask: why do the pipes freeze every winter?
The label has faded. Which jar do you want me to open?
My neighbour keeps asking me, when do they bring the piano upstairs?
The kitchen is tiny. Where does anyone put the plates in there?
The lecturer paused and said, we do measure things that small.
The box says nothing useful. I do fold the tent before it goes in the bag.
The guide is vague on one point: how to pay the toll as a visitor.

notes: Card: ' do' x26 of the top 32, always after How. Probes: 'How do I / how do we / how do you' 0.56-0.58, 'How does' 0.50; 'What do I' 0.20, 'Why do / when do' 0.06, 'I do' 0.00. The word 'how' alone leaks about 0.3 ('How to' 0.31, 'how the' 0.32, 'How did' 0.26), so the near misses mostly use other question words and include one 'how to'. The + pole is the other side of the same distinction: ' to' after How ('How to prevent').
